Fourth, investigate whether the low-rank collapse subspace overlaps with the task semantic subspace for in-context learning.50:T560,The paper defines internalization as a transition from implementing a computation through many explicit steps to implementing it in fewer steps through modified weights. The main empirical setting is semiautomaton simulation. A transformer is trained to generate CoT tokens corresponding to intermediate automaton states over T steps, and then a curriculum progressively removes these CoT tokens so that the model must predict the final state with less explicit computation. This separates learning the step-by-step state transition from compressing the computation. The paper studies task structure through modular counter semiautomata and relates difficulty to the arithmetic structure of the counter order. Counters with small prime-power factors appear easier to represent compactly, while prime-order counters are harder. The theoretical part analyzes sparse parity with a stylized one-layer transformer using linear attention and a fixed nonlinear MLP. The model first learns the hidden-support parity with explicit CoT supervision, then internalizes the autoregressive computation as CoT tokens are removed one at a time, eventually computing the parity directly. The paper also connects the mechanism to Positive Distribution Shift, where the training distribution is deliberately changed in a way that allows earlier learned representations to support later learning.51:T41f,The empirical findings are mainly mechanistic. On semiautomaton tasks, wider transformers internalize CoT more reliably than deeper transformers under a fixed parameter budget. This weakens the simple picture that implicit reasoning is just explicit reasoning unfolded vertically across layers. Task structure matters: among modular counters, prime-order cases are the most difficult to internalize, consistent with the compact-representation argument. Internalization also has a cost. Models that succeed in-distribution often show degraded out-of-distribution performance, suggesting that the compressed computation can become a shortcut rather than a faithful implementation of the original stepwise algorithm. The theoretical sparse-parity result provides the cleanest positive result: explicit CoT makes the hidden computation learnable, and progressive token removal transfers that computation into the direct predictor. The supplied material does not include checkable numerical details such as model sizes, dataset sizes, or exact accuracy deltas.52:T5cb,The authors first isolate a simplified Muon update by removing momentum and Newton-Schulz implementation details. The remaining operation replaces each matrix gradient by its polar factor, keeping singular directions while removing singular values. This isolates the effect of gradient orthogonalization. The theoretical testbed is Burer-Monteiro factorized matrix sensing, which is connected to training two-layer quadratic neural networks and allows the gradient and Hessian geometry to be controlled through the sensing operator. The key model is mixed-spiked matrix sensing. Its sensing operator decomposes into signal, spike, and bulk components. The signal component is task-relevant anisotropy aligned with the ground truth. The spike component is strong but task-irrelevant anisotropy. The bulk component captures the remaining more isotropic directions. This construction mirrors a common feature of LLM training: gradients are highly anisotropic, but not every dominant direction is useful. The authors then analyze the landscape using a river-valley decomposition. The river direction corresponds to meaningful progress toward the ground truth, while hill directions capture sharp transverse deviations. In this geometry, GD quickly descends from the hillside into the river but then makes slow progress along the river. Muon moves rapidly along the sides of the valley, which improves exploration, but its normalized update can prevent fine convergence near the solution.53:T832,方法上分三层。第一层是定义。作者把多轮 MDP 中的状态分成 critical state 和 routine state。critical turn 的动作会改变后续 return distribution；routine turn 虽然是完成任务所必需的执行步骤，但在给定状态下，不同可行动作对最终回报分布近似不变。基于这个划分，decision density ρ 被定义为轨迹中 critical turn 的比例。

第二层是估计器比较。论文比较两类 policy gradient：一类是 turn-level estimator，用每步 advantage A_t 做信用分配，对应 PPO 这一族；另一类是 trajectory-level estimator，用整条轨迹共享的标量优势，对应 GRPO 这一族。关键观察是：在 perfect critic 下，routine turn 的真实 advantage 为 0，因此 turn-level estimator 会逐点把 routine contribution 消掉；而 trajectory-level estimator 只能在期望意义上抵消 routine turn，因为它仍把同一个轨迹级回报乘到这些 turn 的 score function 上，所以会保留额外方差。

第三层是理论推导。作者用 SNR 作为训练步效率代理，分析 turn-level 与 trajectory-level 的信噪比差距。在非退化条件下，perfect critic 情况下 turn-level 相对 trajectory-level 的 SNR 优势按 Θ(ρ^{-1/2}) 增长。也就是说，critical turn 越稀疏，trajectory-level 的浪费越严重。论文还把分析扩展到 imperfect critic：critic 不是免费午餐，若 critic error variance 足够小，turn-level 仍保留优势；但当 critic 误差方差上升到与 decision density 同量级甚至更大时，这种优势会饱和甚至被吃掉。这个扩展很重要，因为它回答了“为什么不是永远上 critic”——因为 critic 的收益要和其误差、成本、稳定性一起看。

实验环境 Diluted Doors 也是技术方案的一部分。它是一个可控 MDP，能精确调节 ρ，同时保持其它因素尽量稳定，用来隔离 signal dilution 机制，而不是在复杂 agent benchmark 上混入太多 confounder。这个设计比直接在真实代码 agent 上做 ablation 更干净。54:T727,The paper proceeds in three steps. First, it defines critical versus routine turns in a finite-horizon MDP. Critical turns are those where the chosen action changes the future return distribution. Routine turns are necessary execution steps, but alternative admissible actions leave the return distribution effectively invariant. Decision density ρ is then defined as the fraction of critical turns in a trajectory.

Second, it compares two policy-gradient families. A turn-level estimator uses per-step advantages A_t, as in PPO-style methods with a value function. Under a perfect critic, routine turns have zero true advantage and are canceled pointwise. A trajectory-level estimator, as in GRPO-style methods, attaches one scalar advantage to the entire trajectory. In that case, routine turns only cancel in expectation, not per sample, so they retain variance contributions.

Third, it derives an SNR comparison. Using signal-to-noise ratio as a proxy for training-step efficiency, the paper shows that under non-degeneracy assumptions, the SNR advantage of turn-level over trajectory-level estimation scales as Θ(ρ^{-1/2}) in the perfect-critic regime. As decision density decreases, the penalty of trajectory-level credit assignment grows. The analysis is then extended to imperfect critics: the turn-level advantage survives only while critic-error variance remains below the scale set by ρ, and saturates once critic noise becomes too large. This extension is important because it explains why adding a critic is not automatically beneficial.

The controlled environment, Diluted Doors, is also part of the technical contribution. It allows the authors to vary ρ directly while keeping other factors as stable as possible, making it easier to isolate the signal-dilution mechanism than in a full LLM-agent benchmark.55:T5ea,The experiments are designed to validate the mechanism rather than to maximize downstream scores. The central testbed is Diluted Doors, a controlled MDP with tunable decision density.

The first key result is an SNR study. Over roughly a 50x range of ρ, the empirical SNR ratio between turn-level and trajectory-level estimators follows the predicted ρ^{-1/2} law extremely closely. The paper reports that the fit explains 99.9% of the variation, which is unusually clean evidence for a theory paper.

The second key result is a training-efficiency study. As ρ decreases, trajectory-level learning becomes increasingly inefficient, while the gap in favor of turn-level estimation widens. This supports the paper’s main claim that the cost of critic-free multi-turn RL is governed by decision density rather than horizon alone.

The paper also discusses the imperfect-critic regime. When critic-error variance is controlled, turn-level estimation retains its advantage; when critic noise grows too large, the gain saturates. If the appendix includes explicit critic-noise sweeps, that part is especially relevant for real LLM RL where value estimation is often unstable.

A limitation is that the empirical evidence is primarily from a controlled MDP, not a full-scale LLM agent training run. So the paper is strong on causal identification and weak on external validity. The next practical question is how to estimate ρ in real agent traces and whether routine versus critical turns can be detected reliably.56:T6b2,Start with the introduction. The two terms to anchor on are signal dilution and decision density. The paper’s main claim is already visible there: the problem in multi-turn RL is not just long horizon, but sparse consequential decisions.

Then read the formal setup and theory sections carefully. Pay attention to how routine states are defined through return-distribution invariance, what exact estimators are being compared, and what assumptions are needed for the SNR scaling result. The usefulness of the conclusion depends on how restrictive those assumptions are.

Next, inspect the construction of Diluted Doors. The important question is whether the environment really varies ρ without simultaneously changing horizon, reward scale, or transition stochasticity. If that control is clean, the empirical validation is much more convincing.

In the experiments, prioritize the figure showing SNR ratio versus ρ and the figure showing training efficiency as ρ changes. One validates the theoretical slope; the other shows that the effect matters for actual learning speed, not just for a derived statistic.

Three follow-up questions are worth carrying into a second pass. First, how could ρ be estimated in real agent tasks from rollouts, tool traces, or verifier signals? Second, can the critic-error-versus-ρ comparison be turned into a practical criterion for whether a critic is worth training? Third, are there cheaper middle-ground solutions—process rewards, step-level verifiers, segment-level return decomposition—that recover some of the benefit without a full critic? A focused read should take around 45 minutes; reading proofs and appendices carefully will take closer to 1.5–2 hours.57:T500,The paper proceeds in two stages. First, it performs a descriptive analysis with anchor-conditioned routing. Repeated anchor token ids are aligned across rollouts, and the corresponding sparse routing vectors are compared to test whether routing still separates problem identity, trajectory context, and effort mode. The authors define three anchor families—trajectory, boundary, and delimiter—and vary the routing readout window around the anchor. Routing representations are built from selected expert ids and router weights across layers, and then analyzed with nearest-neighbor leakage and KNN basin-purity style metrics.

Second, the paper proposes RAD, Routing Agreement Decoding. Given a pool of completed rollouts for one problem, RAD locates a fixed anchor by token id, represents each rollout using the routing window around that anchor, and selects the rollout that lies in the densest Weighted-Jaccard KNN routing neighborhood. During selection, it never parses, normalizes, compares, or executes answer strings. The answer text is only read after the routing-based choice is made. In that sense, RAD is analogous to majority voting in objective, but not in interface: majority aggregates agreement in answer space, while RAD aggregates agreement in routing space.58:T52a,The evaluation covers 10 sparse-MoE configurations and 6 datasets, including gpt-oss and Qwen3-MoE variants, with math, GPQA, LiveCodeBench, and SWE-bench Verified. The results have three main parts. First, identical token ids do not imply identical routing states: routing still separates problem and effort conditions, with reported cross-problem and cross-effort nearest-neighbor leakage below 5%, suggesting token identity is not a sufficient statistic for router state. Second, routing neighborhoods align with final-answer basins, especially near answer-opening delimiters; delimiter@16 gives the strongest basin purity, while even marker-only delimiter@marker is already informative. Third, RAD is roughly on par with textual majority in math and GPQA, slightly ahead in the authors’ rollout pools, while using no answer-string comparison. Its more distinctive use case is code and agentic settings: on code generation, where lexical variation makes exact string voting awkward, RAD can directly select rollouts and report pass@1; on the decidable subset of SWE-bench Verified, boundary-based re-anchoring improves over random selection by about 4–5 points.

The evidence is best read as a feasibility result rather than a universal selector. It depends on access to router traces and on sensible anchor design.59:T6cd,The core method is replay pairing. For a fixed trajectory, the authors run two matched conditions: one keeps the original plan in history, the other replays the same trajectory with the plan removed from history. At each step and layer, they measure cosine distance between hidden states across the two runs. This distance is treated as a plan-fidelity signal. If the model has internalized the plan, removing the text should not quickly change later hidden states. If the model depends on rereading the plan from context, the difference should be large near the plan and then collapse once the plan is no longer actively represented.

They test this on ReAct agents built from Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, replicate within family on Llama-3.1-8B, and compare against DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B. A key methodological contribution is the reasoning-trace confound. In reasoning models, prior <think> blocks often restate the plan. If one removes only the explicit plan text, both replay conditions may still contain plan information, making the measured distance artificially small. Their strict stripping fix removes prior <think> blocks from the plan-removed condition, yielding a cleaner estimate of whether the plan remains available in context.

They also train Ridge probes on hidden states to predict signal magnitude and classify active versus decayed plans. The best layer is L32 in Llama. Probe transfer from Llama to R1 is only partial, and self-probes indicate that R1 uses a substantially different representational direction. The paper is careful about scope: these are representational claims, not strong causal claims about behavior. The authors explicitly note confounds from step index, history length, and discourse structure.5a:T721,On ALFWorld with Llama-3.1-70B, the plan signal peaks at 0.453 one step after the plan is written, then drops by 4.1x within a single action-observation cycle, settling near 0.027 by step +5. On HotpotQA, the decay is even faster at 12.4x. This is the main empirical basis for the claim that plans behave like context-time objects rather than persistent internal state.

The probe analysis is strong numerically but also revealing about confounds. A Ridge probe at L32 predicts signal strength with R^2 = 0.875 and separates active from decayed plans with AUROC 0.999. But step index is also almost perfectly decodable at the same layer, with R^2 = 0.978, so part of the classification power is clearly tied to trajectory phase.

For DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B, naive replay pairing suggests a much smaller step+1 signal than Llama, 0.022 versus 0.099, which would imply weak plan encoding. After strict stripping, the signal increases by 163% in-sample and 153% on held-out data, while Llama changes by only 4.8%, supporting the claim that the original measurement was contaminated by reasoning traces. A Llama-trained L32 probe transferred to strict-stripped R1 states reaches AUROC 0.748 with n = 19 and p = 6e-4. R1 self-probes reach 1.000 AUROC on two distilled families, but along a direction 89.3 degrees away from Llama’s, suggesting near-orthogonal representational geometry.

A compute-routing experiment is only modestly better than fixed-sample self-consistency and worse than a simple output-based baseline. Single-layer activation steering gives mixed results.5d:T942,技术主线有两条：一个算法，一个可识别性理论。

算法部分提出 P-learning，可以看成 Q-learning 的逆问题。普通 Q-learning 在固定环境转移核 P 下，通过 Bellman 更新逼近 Q；P-learning 则把一组固定的 (Q^g, π^g, r^g) 当作观测，迭代更新候选 world model，使它与这些 value functions 的 Bellman 关系越来越一致。作者在 tabular 情形下把这个过程写成线性方程组，并证明收敛到一个由 Moore–Penrose 伪逆给出的解。直观上，Q、policy 和 reward 提供了关于“从状态动作对出发，后继状态分布必须满足什么约束”的大量线性条件；当这些条件足够丰富时，P 就能被唯一识别。文中也说明在很多实际设置里，π 往往由 Q 通过 argmax 或 softmax 导出，因此输入可以近似理解为一组 goal-conditioned Q 和 reward。

理论部分是全文更核心的内容。作者系统分析了在不同 MDP 类型下，什么样的 goal set 能打破 value equivalence。结论分四类。第一，有限状态、确定性 MDP 中，一个“generic” goal 就可能足够识别真实 P。这里 generic 的意思不是任意 goal，而是能让不同后继状态在回报结构上被区分开。第二，有限状态、随机 MDP 中，goals 需要张成状态空间；换句话说，reward family 必须足够丰富，才能把随机转移分布的自由度约束住。第三，确定性连续状态情形里，有限个 goals 有时也足够，这一点有些反直觉，因为连续空间通常让人预期需要无限监督。第四，随机连续 MDP 中，关键不再是 goal 的个数，而是 coverage：对 Gaussian rewards，需要 goal set 有非空内点；对 indicator rewards，需要覆盖状态空间。作者还给出当 Q 只有 ε 近似精度时，恢复出的 P 的误差界，说明 world model 的准确性会随 value 误差平滑退化，而不是脆弱崩掉。

这套方法与传统 world model learning 的区别在于，它不直接拟合转移样本，而是从 agent 已经学到的价值结构中反演环境。与 successor features、forward-backward learning、一般 goal-conditioned RL 的关系则是：这些方法原本被视为多目标 value learning，这篇论文说明在目标集足够丰富时，它们携带的信息量其实接近显式动力学模型。5e:T86d,The paper has two technical pillars: P-learning as an inversion algorithm, and identifiability results that characterize when inversion is possible.

P-learning is introduced as an inverse analogue of Q-learning. In standard Q-learning, the transition kernel is fixed and Bellman updates are used to estimate values. Here the values, policies, and rewards are treated as given, and the transition model is updated so that the Bellman equations become increasingly consistent with those fixed quantities. In the tabular setting, this becomes a structured linear inverse problem, and the paper proves convergence to a solution expressed through the Moore–Penrose pseudoinverse. Intuitively, each tuple (Q^g, pi^g, r^g) imposes constraints on what the next-state distribution must be for every state-action pair. If the goal family is rich enough, those constraints pin down the true kernel.

The more fundamental part is the identifiability theory. The paper characterizes when value equivalence can be broken in four regimes. In deterministic finite MDPs, a single generic goal can be sufficient to identify the true dynamics. In stochastic finite MDPs, the reward family must span the state space; otherwise the stochastic degrees of freedom remain hidden behind equivalent values. In deterministic continuous MDPs, somewhat surprisingly, a finite number of goals can still suffice in some cases. In stochastic continuous MDPs, the key notion is coverage rather than cardinality: for Gaussian rewards, the goal set needs non-empty interior; for indicator rewards, it must cover the state space. The paper also provides error bounds showing that if the Q-functions are only epsilon-accurate, the recovered model degrades gracefully rather than catastrophically.

This differs from standard world-model learning because the method does not fit transitions directly from rollouts. Instead, it extracts dynamics from the value structure already learned by the agent. It also reframes goal-conditioned RL, successor-feature style methods, and related approaches as potentially implicit model-learning procedures when the goal family is sufficiently expressive.5f:T6d3,The experiments ask two main questions: can P-learning recover accurate world models in practice, and are the recovered models useful beyond the training goals?

For finite MDPs, the paper validates the theory on three FourRooms variants: deterministic, windy, and teleporting. As stochasticity increases, the number of goals needed for near-perfect recovery also increases. The headline numbers are that |G| = 1, 4, and 20 goals are sufficient, respectively, for quasi-perfect recovery in those three settings. This aligns well with the theory: deterministic environments need much less reward diversity than stochastic ones.

In continuous control, the paper studies Reacher and finds that only |G| = 4 goals are enough to recover an accurate implicit world model. A notable result is that the recovered model is accurate even on variables that the reward never directly depends on. Planning inside the recovered model then transfers to out-of-distribution goals, including angular-velocity targets despite training only on position-based goals. That is a strong sign that the agent has internalized more than a narrow reward-specific shortcut.

The MountainCar experiments probe this implicit generalization further. Training on velocity-based goals instead of position-based goals yields an almost identical recovered world model, suggesting that agents optimized for very different objectives may still internalize similar dynamics. Finally, the paper reports a very strong correlation between agent performance and recovered world-model accuracy, with Spearman rho = 0.98. This does not establish causality, but it supports the view that successful goal-conditioned value learning is often accompanied by accurate implicit dynamics learning.60:T4e2,Setup: 28 Reddit communities (17 mental-health, 11 controls). They compare Qwen3 embedding models at 0.6B and 4B in two regimes: zero-shot pretrained encoder embeddings and supervised fine-tuned embeddings (encoder trained with a linear classifier on community labels).
Core analyses:
- RSA with category prototypes: average document embeddings per category, build a cosine-distance RDM, and compute Spearman correlation with an expert symptom-relationship RDM. A domain-control RDM is used to separate expert-structure alignment from a coarse mental-health vs control split. Significance via label permutation; uncertainty via bootstrap over documents.
- Local geometry probes: prototype-based typicality (within-class centrality), prototype margins (boundary confusions when margin < 0), and a boundary-alignment score that tests whether residual ambiguity concentrates on expert-neighbor category pairs.
- Multi-baseline confound controls: compare geometry against affect (VAD), LIWC, stylistic, and topic-based baselines to attribute what drives alignment.
Design choice: prototype/RDM lifts evaluation to category-structure level (less noisy), while local probes explain what contributes to RSA rather than reporting a single opaque correlation.61:T407,TAS, Temporal Attractor Steering, has three stages. First, a lightweight detector estimates whether a query is likely to exhibit PTC, so steering is gated rather than applied globally. Second, causal activation patching identifies a conflict-critical layer for a model family, i.e. a layer where replacing residual-stream activations most reliably flips the answer between old and new facts. Third, if the detector score exceeds a threshold, TAS perturbs the residual stream at that layer along a steering direction toward the newer-fact representation. A central detail is the knowledge-recovery filter: a record is counted as PTC only if the newer answer has sufficient average log probability under a temporally cued prompt, with τ_rec = -3. This prevents the benchmark from mixing recoverable conflicts with cases where the model simply lacks the updated fact. Compared with generic activation steering such as ITI, TAS is conflict-gated, temporally targeted, and explicitly evaluated for preservation on non-conflict records.62:T434,Skin-Deep compares an aligned model M with its base counterpart M0. For harmful-request prompts and length-matched benign instructions, it extracts final-token residual-stream activations at each layer. It first uses contrastive PCA to find candidate directions that separate harmful requests from benign instructions by comparing activation covariance in the aligned and base models. It then measures separation with Cohen’s d. PERMANOVA and RBF-kernel MMD are used as full-space validation checks, so the signal is not only a one-dimensional projection artifact. Additional controls include PCA on unit-normalized activations to rule out pure norm effects and cosine comparison with the Arditi refusal direction to test whether the recovered directions collapse to a known refusal axis. The causal step is direction ablation during generation: selected peak-layer directions are removed and compared with random-direction controls. The layer-wise pattern is then compressed into the Geometric Fragility Score, computed before the tested LoRA or attack intervention is run.63:T416,The study evaluates 21 models across six alignment recipes, with sizes from 3B to 32B. The main empirical findings are: harmful and benign prompts separate along a small number of hidden-state directions; split-sample checks show that layer selection transfers to held-out prompts; full-space PERMANOVA and MMD support that the split is not merely a projection artifact; unit-norm controls reduce the chance that the signal is just activation magnitude. Direction ablation weakens refusal in models where a measurable drop is available, while random controls do not show the same effect. The refusal-changing directions differ by model, suggesting model-specific directions inside a recurring low-rank safety geometry rather than one universal refusal vector. Cross-family checks show similar activation relationships among the same prompts, but the strongest harmful/general separation appears at different layers. In the LoRA experiment, GFS identifies the initially safe model that retains the most refusal under the small-scale LoRA protocol.64:T40e,The method treats the contextual hidden states of prompt tokens at each transformer layer as a point cloud. It then computes finite zero-dimensional persistent homology, H0, for each layer. H0 tracks how disconnected components merge as the distance threshold grows, giving a compact view of the connectivity structure among token representations. Each layer is summarized by three descriptors: mean finite lifetime, normalized lifetime entropy, and the concentration ratio of the largest lifetimes. Concatenating these descriptors across layers gives a low-dimensional topology vector for the question. This vector is used for detection and also for steering. For steering, the method retrieves topologically similar positive and negative examples for the current query, constructs a local contrast direction in activation space, and applies the intervention during prefill or decoding. The important design choice is that topology selects the local comparison set, while the actual edit remains in the model’s native activation space.65:T5fd,The main contribution is Ledger Residuals. A standard pre-norm transformer has a single width-d residual stream that every sublayer reads from and writes to. Ledger Residuals factor this into two width-d streams. The Deliberation stream D is a scratchpad: sublayers can write to it freely and can also erase stale content. The Commitment stream C is an append-only ledger: sublayers may commit information into it through a gate, but cannot overwrite what is already there, and the unembedding reads only from C. Initialization is D0 = embed(x) and C0 = 0. Each sublayer produces both an update to D and a gated contribution to C. The design is intentionally asymmetric: D is where computation happens, C is where the model stores the representation it will be judged on. Importantly, the architecture reduces to a standard pre-norm transformer at a known gate setting, so it serves as a controlled instrument rather than a completely unrelated model family. The causal test is straightforward. If massive activations are just a workaround for the residual stream’s dual role, then a protected decode-only channel should make them unnecessary. The authors also add a commit-sparsity penalty to encourage selective use of C, hoping to keep the commitment channel clean. Instead, stronger sparsity pressure makes the rebuilt outlier more persistent and more concentrated. That is the key technical result: the model actively recreates the feature in the readout channel rather than passively inheriting it from a flawed architecture.66:T523,The experiments are modest in scale but well controlled. The authors train language models at 160M and 290M parameters and compare Ledger Residuals against standard transformers at matched loss, so the mechanistic conclusions are not confounded by large performance gaps. Three findings matter most. First, a protected decode-only commitment channel does not remove massive activations. The model rebuilds the canonical fixed-dimension outlier in C, and it remains strongly concentrated on the sequence-start token. Second, the rebuilt outlier is somewhat smaller in magnitude than in a standard transformer, but it is more sharply localized in both dimension and position. So the phenomenon is not gone; it is reorganized under the new architectural constraints. Third, the obvious remedy backfires. With stronger commit-sparsity regularization, dominant-dimension persistence rises from 0.58 to 0.96, and start-token concentration rises from 3.4 to 4.7. In other words, the model does not reduce reliance on the outlier channel; it makes that channel more stable and more focused. The paper emphasizes structural measurements rather than benchmark scores: activation magnitude distributions, persistence of the dominant dimension across layers, and concentration on the start token under matched-loss comparisons.67:T45d,For a skim, start with the Introduction to understand the two competing hypotheses: artifact versus function. Then go straight to Section 3 and Figure 1, which explain the Deliberation/Commitment split and why it is a meaningful controlled intervention. After that, read Section 5 carefully. The most informative plots are the ones showing activation magnitude, dominant-dimension persistence, and start-token concentration. The ablation with commit-sparsity penalty is especially important because it shows that making the commitment channel cleaner does not remove the outlier; it strengthens it. If you only have about 25 minutes, read the Introduction, Section 3, Section 5, and the conclusion. If you want more depth, compare this paper mentally with prior approaches such as key/value biasing, QK normalization, and gated softmax variants. Those works show that outliers can sometimes be suppressed without immediate loss collapse. This paper tests a stronger claim: when the architecture is changed to provide a dedicated readout channel, does the model still choose to recreate the outlier? The answer is yes.68:T4e8,A three-regime taxonomy is proposed under the thesis that channel location determines auditability. Two key constructs are defined: a screen is any quantity computed before training that predicts transfer magnitude; a carrier is the component whose removal, replacement, or neutralization abolishes transfer. The three regimes are: 1) Initialization-dependent body channel: traits transfer via activation patterns in non-output weights, predictable before training by coverage — the cosine similarity between the student's first distillation gradient step and the teacher's fine-tuning displacement vector; 2) Convergent unembedding / vocabulary geometry channel: single-token traits in pretrained LLMs transfer probability mass via high-cosine neighbours in the output matrix, independent of initialization, so all initialization-alignment screens including coverage fail; 3) A single pretrained model can host both channels, and the active channel is a property of the signal rather than the model — conditional behaviours route through the body channel, while single-token preferences route through readout geometry. A relocation experiment that randomizes the readout restores initialization gating, confirming channel location is signal-dependent.69:T404,Starting from the established key-value memory interpretation of vanilla FFNs, the work first proves that static or per-pair query projections can be absorbed into the key matrix without increasing expressivity. To unlock additional capacity, dynamically computing per-pair queries and keys from input tokens is required, but this is parameter-prohibitive for large hidden dimensions. A rank-1 outer product approximation of each per-pair QK^T matrix recovers exactly the elementwise multiplicative form of gated MLPs. The work further proves that applying nonlinear activation to one branch (the query branch) before multiplication breaks two symmetries of the unmodified rank-1 formulation: (1) query-key exchange symmetry, broken by any nonlinear activation (only linear activations preserve it); (2) inverse-scaling symmetry, broken by non-homogeneous activations such as SiLU and GELU (ReLU preserves it for positive scaling factors due to positive homogeneity). A rank-R generalization of the formulation is also proposed.6a:T419,The empirical section stresses three tests. On a closed-form anchor, lambda_min^+(G) collapses by about 246x at the bottleneck layer carrying a dead direction, while a dimension-fixed boundary layer remains flat. For multiple dead directions, log det^+(G_l) scales with rank deficit: across 7 noisy-bridge configurations with L in {4,6,8}, D in {20,50}, full-batch and mini-batch SGD, 5 seeds, and r=1..4, the slope ratios for r=2,3,4 are 2.0, 3.1, and 4.0, close to the predicted 2, 3, and 4; the single smallest positive eigenvalue is largely insensitive to r. On the Aoyagi 2005 anchor with analytic RLCT values in the range 9 to 25, calibrated LLC recovers about 99% of the target lambda, while DDS rate-chain observables rank-track lambda with |rho| between 0.95 and 0.98. A naive H*r capacity proxy also reaches 0.99, so that experiment is a sanity check rather than a discriminating result. An off-anchor nonlinear transformer probe keeps the predicted structural sign but loses the trajectory-rate relation, which is an important limitation.6b:T42c,Fugu is a family of learned orchestrators exposed through a single model interface. Given a user query, it constructs an agentic scaffold over a pool of frontier LLM workers: which workers to call, what roles or instructions they receive, how they interact with tools or environments, how intermediate outputs are checked, and how the final response is synthesized. The report describes two operating points. Fugu is optimized for speed and selects a single worker per input, aiming for latency close to a direct frontier-model call while improving query-specific routing. Fugu-Ultra is optimized for quality and can compose multiple agents per input, trading additional latency for better performance on complex tasks. This differs from static ensembling and simple winner-take-all routing because the scaffold itself is generated by a model and may include decomposition, role assignment, communication, verification, and synthesis. The worker pool can also be configured around provider, privacy, compliance, or user constraints without retraining the orchestrator.6c:T41a,The report claims that Fugu exceeds individual publicly accessible frontier workers on a range of engineering, scientific, and reasoning benchmarks, and is competitive with Fable 5 and Mythos Preview on several rigorous evaluations. The key claim for Fugu is that single-worker learned routing can match or surpass strong direct calls at comparable latency. The key claim for Fugu-Ultra is that multi-agent composition improves quality on harder tasks by combining specializations. The provided text explicitly mentions software-engineering benchmarks, scientific tasks, reasoning tasks, and the abstract points to SWE-style evaluations. It does not provide per-benchmark scores, confidence intervals, cost-normalized curves, or ablation numbers in the supplied content. The critical experimental checks are whether the worker pool contains the compared systems, whether routing data overlaps benchmark styles, how Fugu-Ultra is normalized for extra calls and tokens, and whether the multi-agent gain remains after compute and latency are controlled.6d:T79d,AdaMem centers on a structured Memory Policy. The policy is a JSON object that maps each character or role C_i to a natural-language extraction preference T_i, such as keeping only final business decisions and deadlines while ignoring casual chatter. The system then runs a weekly closed loop with four stages.

First is Daily Extraction. New conversations are processed by an extractor LLM, but the extraction prompt is conditioned on the current policy rather than using a generic save-everything rule. The paper also adds Time Anchoring: the prompt includes the absolute session date and instructs the model to resolve relative expressions like “tomorrow” into absolute dates before storing them. That is a small but important systems detail, because relative temporal references decay quickly in long-term memory.

Second is Weekly Evaluation. At the end of each week, the system is probed with QA examples targeting preference-aligned information.

Third is Policy Reflection. Errors are diagnosed into two categories. Recall Failure means the relevant information appeared in dialogue but was never written, so the policy is too restrictive. Precision Failure means irrelevant retrieved memories polluted the answer, so the policy is too permissive. Based on these failures, the model generates a policy patch rather than rewriting the full policy from scratch. This patch-style update is easier to inspect and easier to roll back.

Fourth is Failure Rollback and Policy Rendering. If the updated policy hurts validation performance on historical QA pairs, the change is rejected and the system reverts to the previous policy. The accepted policy is then rendered into extraction instructions for the next week. The interesting part here is not a new neural architecture but a control loop: write policy, evaluate, diagnose, patch, validate, and only then deploy. That makes the method easy to insert into existing RAG-style memory stacks.6e:T6f7,The evaluation includes both a new benchmark and the method comparison itself. The benchmark, AdaMem-Bench, is designed specifically for preference-guided long-horizon memory. It uses multi-session dialogues over multiple weeks, multiple concurrent personas, and deliberately overlapping semantic content across characters so that the system must avoid confusing similar but irrelevant memories. Each session is annotated with golden memories: atomic facts that match the character’s preference profile are labeled as relevant, while the rest is treated as noise. That setup is better aligned with the paper’s goal than generic QA benchmarks.

Empirically, the paper reports up to +9.0% QA accuracy while reducing memory volume by 9%, across two extractor LLMs and two feedback modes. That combination matters more than the accuracy number alone, because it suggests the gains come from better selectivity rather than from simply storing more information. The analysis says improvements are concentrated in soft-preference categories such as emotions, promises, and schedules. That is plausible: these are exactly the categories where a uniform extraction rule tends to either miss subtle information or over-store irrelevant details. The main remaining bottleneck is policy inference from weak feedback, meaning the system can observe that an answer failed but cannot always infer the right policy adjustment.

When reading the experiments, the most useful questions are practical ones: what the baselines are, how memory volume is measured, how often rollback is triggered, and whether the gains hold across different extractor models. If the paper includes error-type breakdowns by recall versus precision failure, those are likely more informative than the top-line QA score.6f:T41a,Two pillars:
1) TMAX-15K environment generation: instead of only generating trajectories, they synthesize full terminal RL environment instances using a strong frontier model. A taxonomy drives generation with explicit difficulty control, persona variation (to diversify constraints and narrative framing), and verifier diversification (to avoid brittle binary checks). Some tasks use continuous-valued rewards rather than pass/fail.
2) RL recipe (TMAX): built on an asynchronous RL stack (open-instruct). They report naive GRPO becoming unstable in long-horizon agent settings, and switch to DPPO (Divergence Proximal Policy Optimization). Two emphasized stabilizers are an FP32 LM head (to mitigate mixed-precision numerical issues around logits/softmax/entropy/KL) and a large group size (lower-variance advantage estimates and smoother updates).

For many tokens, early layers make a rough guess, intermediate layers stabilize the reasoning-relevant semantics, and the last few layers can then shift the distribution toward generic, alignment-favored, or pragmatically safer continuations. The authors call this pattern Guess–Refine–Perturb. The actual problem is therefore not early exiting for efficiency, but how to choose, at each generation step, the most reliable near-final layer for emission without changing model weights or truncating the forward pass.","importance":"Its value for foundation-model research is twofold. Second, the proposed decoding rule is training-free and parameter-free. If the phenomenon is real and robust, part of the so-called alignment tax may be recoverable at inference time rather than only through new training objectives. Existing options each fail on one axis. Full-context prompting preserves fidelity but scales poorly in latency and KV cache. RAG and text-memory systems keep growing external stores and operate in discrete text space, which is good for exact recall but weak at abstracting evolving preferences. Starting from a high-quality reference response, the framework applies a controlled degradation to create a worse response, and defines the gold label as preferring the original reference. This produces pairwise items from any reference corpus without human annotation. The perturbations are designed to be language-agnostic, relying on whitespace tokens, sentence boundaries, and digit patterns. The repeat_pad perturbation is the verbosity-bias probe: it makes the degraded response longer while keeping it strictly worse, so a preference for the padded response indicates a length bias. 不是单一 retrieval 指标，至少要区分静态保留、动态覆写、隐式偏好归纳、跨 app 实体绑定。第二，随着历史增长，系统退化未必体现在最终服务任务上，可能先体现在内部状态重建上，这对训练目标设计和 memory interface 设计都有意义。第三，作者的误差归因显示 93% 以上失败来自 memory retrieval 而不是 answer 用于基于该状态做服务决策。这样可以区分“记住了什么”和“能否用出来”。第三，画像演化不是随机漂移，而是由 season、major life event、circumstance shift 等外部原因触发，并允许一个原因同时推动多类状态联动变化，例如冬季健身计划同时改变装备、作息和消费偏好。第四，评测不是单点，而是在 15 个月轨迹上的 5 个季度 checkpoint 做分段测试，观察历史变长后系统如何退化，以及是否能正确覆盖旧值。这个设计比单次 full-history accuracy 更接近真实长期记忆系统的需求。论文还评测了五类代表性 memory systems。虽然你给出的全文片段没有完整方法细节，但从作者的分析看，他们把系统拆成 memory retrieval 与 answer model 两部分，并做了 failure 项，以及 383 个带因果标注的状态转移；最终形成 3,634 个 checkpoint-based problems 和 4,994 个细粒度评分点。主要实验结论有三条。第一，随着历史增长，State Completion 准确率持续下降，而 Personalized Service 没有同等幅度下降，说明系统可能还能在服务任务上“蒙对”或依赖局部线索，但内部用户状态表征已经开始失真。第二，没有任何一个系统能同时做好两件事：保留仍然为真的事实，以及覆盖已经变化的事实。也就是说，当前 memory system 往往在 retention 和 overwrite 之间存在明显张力。第三，错误集中在两类更难的记忆对象上：隐式偏好，以及需要精确实体绑定的属性，比如具体工作工具、具体品牌或对象名称。最重要的误差归因结果是，超过 93% 的失败来自 memory retrieval，而不是 answer Existing memory benchmarks mostly use short dialogues or isolated events, so they fail to test cross-app consistency, causal profile evolution, and the overwrite-vs-retain behavior required in realistic long-horizon memory systems.","importance":"Its main value is as evaluation infrastructure, not as a new training method. 往往只测概念题，或者只测一般性的工具调用，难以覆盖真实统计工作里“选方法—调参数—跑工具—解释结果—写成分析结论”这一整条链路。论文把问题拆成两个层面：一是封闭式统计知识与程序化操作能力，二是开放式、接近建模竞赛的端到端统计分析能力。更具体地说，它要回答的不是“模型会不会背统计学”，而是“模型能不能在有工具的前提下，稳定完成真实统计分析任务”。","importance":"对预训练研究的意义主要不在于提出新训练方法，而在于提供了一个较干净的能力切面：统计分析是典型的高知识密度、强工具依赖、强程序约束任务，能较好地区分语言表面流畅性与真正的结构化分析能力。这个 practical application 做成“问题 + 数据集 + 工具参数真值”的三元组，让模型必须调用 SAToolKit 才能完成任务。SAToolKit 提供 35 个可调用统计函数，覆盖描述统计、假设检验、回归、因果、生存分析、高维分析等主题。这样评测的不是自由发挥，而是：模型能否选对函数、填对参数、理解输出。\n\n数据构建上，作者从教材、已有 benchmark、公开考试与资源库中收集题目，然后做 modify-and-verify 流程来降低污染风险。具体做法是先用 Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct 和 Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct 试答；若题目被正确答出，则视为潜在泄漏样本，人工改写题干、扰动选项、翻转真假条件等，再次验证，只有至少一个模型失败或经专家确认质量足够的样本才保留。这个流程并不完美，但比简单去重更贴近“语义层面的去污染”。\n\nStat-Open 则是 30 个开放式统计建模任务，来自 MCM/ICM、CUMCM、MAS 框架；开放题则用不同建模框架生成报告，再交给 judge 打分。整体上，这篇工作更像是在构建一个“统计分析能力测试台”，而不是单纯出一套题。","experiments":"关键结果有几组。第一，Stat-Closed 上，即便 GPT-5.1 也只有 68.6% 准确率，最强开源模型 Qwen2.5-72B 为 60.6%。这说明在有工具可用的情况下，统计分析仍不是接近解决的问题。第二，Stat-Open 上，最佳 agent framework 的平均分是 61.86，说明开放式端到端建模更难，瓶颈不只是知识，还包括任务分解、工具编排和结果表达。第三，作者使用 Friedman test 给出显著性结果 p = 2.87 × Certifiable evaluation answers this question by providing guarantee for LLM evaluation. However, existing methods are not generally anytime-valid: the cla","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-06-18T18:07:42Z","category_id":"eval","cover_url":"/covers/2606_20820.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.LG"],"summary":{"core_problem":"CELEUS 解决的是顺序式 LLM 评测里的统计有效性问题：评测者一边抽样、一边更新置信区间，并可能在区间足够窄时停止；如果置信区间不是 anytime-valid，反复查看和自适应停止会破坏名义覆盖率。已有方法在实践中还会用已评测样本更新分层或采样策略，形成同一批数据既用于决策又用于不确定性估计的 double dipping。","importance":"对预训练研究的直接启发在评测侧。基座模型评测越来越依赖大规模题库、模型裁判、人类偏好和开放生成评分，单次固定样本评测很难兼顾成本和置信度。CELEUS 把顺序评测、主动选样和统计覆盖率放到同一个框架里，适合用于模型 checkpoint 选择、数据配比实验、训练中期能力追踪，以及昂贵评测集上的早停决策。贡献不在模型训练方法，而在让自适应评测的置信声明更可执行。","technical_approach":"方法核心是用 e-process 构造 anytime-valid 置信区间。e-process 的优点是对应用侧要求较弱，主要需要评分有界，通常可通过归一化或截断满足。难点在于评测样本不是均匀抽取，而是由不确定性引导采样；未评测样本还会用 surrogate score 近似。如果直接用观测风险，会对目标总体风险产生偏差。CELEUS 的处理是先构造 surrogate-completed 的有限池风险估计：已评测样本用真实风险，未评测样本用代理分数。新样本被选中并获得真实风险后，再加入 inverse-probability-weighted residual correction，即按被选概率校正该样本真实风险与代理分数的残差。这样得到的顺序信号在条件意义下对有限池风险无偏，随后通过 test inversion 得到 anytime-valid CI。对总体风险，方法再加一个 Hoeffding-style correction，把有限池结论提升到 population risk；当池子很大时该修正较小，小池子则可退化为全量评测。","experiments":"给定内容主要展示理论设计和有效性论证，而不是完整实验表格。可确认的结果包括：Theorem 3 给出条件无偏性，这是 e-process CI 成立的关键；Theorem 4 和 Theorem 5 分析 surrogate 分数与样本选择如何降低方差，并给出 oracle variance-optimal sampling rule，作为经验性 uncertainty-guided sampling 的依据；另有 anytime-valid 覆盖率证明。具体模型、数据集、样本节省比例和覆盖率数值在提供材料中不可核验。","reading_guide":"泛读建议用 20 到 30 分钟。重点看 Introduction 里对 Cer-Eval 式做法的 double dipping 诊断，以及 Section 4 的信号构造和 Theorem 3。若只关心能否用于实际评测，直接看 surrogate-completed estimate、IPW residual correction、finite-pool 到 population 的 Hoeffding 修正。若关心成本节省，再看方差分析和采样规则。实验部分若有完整版本，优先检查两点：自适应停止后的真实覆盖率是否接近标称值；在同等 CI 宽度下能少评多少样本。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"CELEUS targets a statistical gap in sequential LLM evaluation. Evaluators often keep sampling, updating confidence intervals, and stopping once the interval is narrow enough. Standard fixed-time confidence intervals do not remain valid under repeated monitoring and adaptive stopping. Existing adaptive evaluation methods can also reuse the same evaluated data to update partitions or sampling rules and to quantify uncertainty, which creates a double-use problem.","importance":"The contribution is mainly on evaluation methodology, but it matters for pretraining workflows. Large model development increasingly relies on expensive open-ended evaluations, model-judge scores, human preference labels, and large item pools. A valid sequential evaluation procedure can support checkpoint selection, data-mixture comparisons, mid-training monitoring, and early stopping of costly evaluations without making overconfident claims.","technical_approach":"The framework builds anytime-valid confidence intervals through e-processes. The application-side assumption is mild: evaluation scores need to be bounded, which can usually be enforced by normalization or clipping. The main technical issue is bias under non-uniform adaptive sampling. CELEUS constructs a conditionally unbiased signal for the finite-pool risk. At each round, it forms a surrogate-completed estimate using observed scores for evaluated items and surrogate scores for unevaluated items. After an uncertainty-guided sampler selects a new item and its true score is observed, CELEUS adds an inverse-probability-weighted correction for the residual between the true score and the surrogate score. This corrected sequential signal enables e-process-based test inversion. A Hoeffding-style correction then lifts finite-pool intervals to population-risk intervals.","experiments":"The provided content primarily contains the framework and theoretical claims. A base reward combines answer correctness and a light format term. A grounding penalty, scaled by a scalar λ, fires only when the model answers correctly on a clean video but produces the same answer on a temporally perturbed video — i.e., when it answered correctly without using temporal visual content. This pushes the policy toward answers that are both correct and genuinely video-dependent. A visual-hacking score (VHS) quantifies shortcut reliance by measuring answer invariance to a task-relevant visual perturbation. (1) Shortcut onset is sharp and seed-robust: reliance rises abruptly over a narrow window of optimization steps, with nearly identical onset curves across two independent random seeds. (2) Shortcut plateau level is a monotone function of λ, with a formation–reversal asymmetry: at an intermediate λ, the trajectory first forms a strong shortcut and then spontaneously reverses it later in training, analogous to hysteresis in driven systems. (3) A critical intervention window exists: applying the grounding penalty before onset suppresses shortcut formation, whereas the same penalty applied after consolidation is substantially less effective at reversal. Identical or similar observations are grouped into state groups, and actions become edges between source and destination states. State value is estimated by aggregating outcomes over all states in the same group, instead of relying on one trajectory’s terminal reward. Action advantage is then computed from the value increment across an edge, which resembles a one-step TD error in sparse-reward tasks. Unlike local group methods such as GiGPO, which compare actions only within the same state, G2PO normalizes edge-level TD errors against a global reference group containing transitions from the whole graph. Standard RL trains a model to produce one strong reasoning trace. In deployment, however, practitioners often use parallel sampling, search over multiple candidates, aggregation, verification, and revision. The model is not trained to coordinate these compute primitives, so additional inference compute is often wasted on redundant traces or weak aggregation.","importance":"The work is relevant to the pretrain-posttrain interface rather than to tokenizer, data mixture, or architecture. It treats test-time scaling behavior as a trainable object. The key implication is that reasoning ability depends not only on the quality of a single chain of thought, but also on whether the model has learned the topology of inference compute: sequential thinking, parallel exploration, and cross-trace aggregation. This is a useful direction for RL pretraining and reasoning-oriented mid-training, especially if future training recipes aim to optimize models for the way they will actually be served.","technical_approach":"SPIRAL stands for Sequential-Parallel-Aggregative Reinforcement Learning. It exposes the model to three forms of inference compute during training: sequential compute inside one trace, parallel compute across independently sampled traces, and aggregative compute that synthesizes a set of traces into a final output. Aggregation traces can be optimized with standard RL algorithms such as GRPO because they generate a final answer that receives a reward. Parallel traces require a different credit assignment scheme: an individual trace may be wrong, but still contain an idea that helps the aggregator solve the problem. SPIRAL uses set reinforcement learning, where a set of generations from the same prompt receives a joint learning signal. A low-variance marginal advantage is then used to assign credit to individual traces under the set-level objective. This differs from standard GRPO, which optimizes the relative advantage of individual responses rather than the utility of a candidate set plus an aggregator.","experiments":"The paper fine-tunes Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on mathematical reasoning and compares SPIRAL against GRPO under an equal training compute budget. The main empirical claim is that SPIRAL improves the model’s ability to use multiple samples and aggregation, rather than only improving single-trace reasoning. Many current systems use chain-of-thought traces, step labels, verifier rewards, or reranking as if intermediate text and intermediate representations were reliable evidence of reasoning. A representation can encode verifier labels with high accuracy, and can even show causal effects under activation patching, while the generated prose remains unfaithful. The model emits a sequence containing a natural-language rationale and an explicit inline claim. A programmatic verifier, such as a theorem prover, game engine, code oracle, or evidence labeler, produces a target label or scalar for that claim. The hidden states over the rationale span are mean-pooled and passed to a linear consistency head, which predicts the verifier target. Training combines the usual language-modeling objective with this consistency loss. The design differs from outcome-level verification, where the verifier only checks final answers, reranks samples, or trains a reward model. Here the verifier signal is attached to a particular rationale span. The estimation error of rational value risk is decomposed into three independent components: candidate approximation error from finite sample sets, prompt sampling error from limited evaluation prompts, and verification error from imperfect judges or verifiers. 轨迹，构造两个匹配条件：A 保留历史中的原始 plan；B 在重放同一轨迹时把 plan 从历史里移除。然后在每一步、每一层比较两条件 hidden state 的 cosine distance，把它当作 plan-fidelity signal。若模型真的把 plan 内化，那么删掉 plan 文本后，后续 hidden state 不应立刻大幅变化；若模型依赖每步重读 plan，则距离会在 plan 仍可见时显著、随后快速衰减。\n\n作者先在 Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct 的 ReAct agent 上做主实验，再在 Llama-3.1-8B 和 DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-70B 上做复现与对照。一个关键技术点是他们发现 reasoning model 的 <think> trace 会污染测量：即便删掉显式 plan，旧的思维链里仍会重复 plan 内容，导致 A/B 两条件都还带着 plan 信息，距离被低估。为此他们提出 strict stripping，只在 B 条件中移除先前 <think> block，以更干净地测“plan 是否还在上下文里”。\n\n除了直接看 hidden-state distance，作者还训练 Ridge probe 去预测 plan signal 强度，并区分 active plan 与 decayed plan。探针在 Llama 的峰值层 L32 上效果最好。作者也做了 probe transfer：用 Llama 上训练的 probe 去测 R1 strict-stripped hidden states，发现仍有一定可迁移性，但方向差异很大，说明不同模型家族编码 plan 的表征子空间并不一致。\n\n这篇工作的边界也交代得比较清楚：它主要是 representational claim，不是强因果行为结论。作者承认 cosine distance 会混入 step index、长度、话语结构等因素；他们也指出 step index 在同层几乎可被完美解码，因此 probe 的高 AUROC 不能简单理解为“纯 plan 内容检测”。","experiments":"主结果来自 ALFWorld 和 HotpotQA。Llama-3.1-70B 上，plan signal 在写完 plan 后的下一步达到 0.453，随后一个 action-observation cycle 内下降 4.1 倍，到 step +5 附近稳定在约 0.027。HotpotQA 衰减更快，达到 12.4 倍量级。这个结果支持“plan 主要靠上下文保留，而不是 hidden state 持久保存”。\n\n探针实验里，L32 的 Ridge probe 对 signal 强度预测达到 R^2=0.875，区分 active/decayed plan 的 AUROC 为 0.999；但同层 step index 的可解码性也很高，R^2=0.978，说明这里有明显混杂。\n\n在 reasoning model 上，若不处理 <think> 污染，R1 的 step+1 signal 只有 0.022，而 Llama 为 0.099，看起来像是 R1 几乎不编码 plan。strict stripping 后，R1 的信号在样本内提升 163%，留出集提升 153%，而对非 reasoning 的 Llama 只带来 4.8% 变化，说明这个修正主要是在消除 trace contamination。Llama 训练的 L32 probe 迁移到 R1 strict-stripped states 上，n=19 时 AUROC 0.748，p=6×10^-4；R1 自探针在两个 distilled family 上可到 1.000，但与 Llama 的方向夹角约 89.3°，说明表征方向几乎正交。\n\n行为层面，作者做了一个压缩压力测试：naive plan eviction 会让 ALFWorld 成功率下降 34.7 个百分点，而 probe-gated re-surfacing 不能恢复，说明“检测到 plan 变弱再补救”并不容易。另一方面，strict stripping 对任务成功率影响小且不显著，L32 的统一 steering 也是 null result，这进一步说明论文主张集中在表征层，而不是已经证明了简单干预就能改进行为。","reading_guide":"泛读时先看 Introduction 和 Existing work relies on single-perspective explanations such as persona shifts or catastrophic forgetting; the work decomposes EM through three core SFT components: training dynamics, model priors, and representational associations between training and evaluation data, addressing unstudied gaps including quantitative links between in-domain training loss and out-of-domain alignment, feasibility of inducing local minima with less broad misalignment via learning schedule tuning, fine-grained alignment score correlations between pre-trained and misaligned models, and the role of prompt representation subspace overlap in driving misalignment generalization.","importance":"Provides empirical guidance for safety design in the pretrain-posttrain closed loop. bloat}","starred":false,"priority":"p2","reading_tier":"skim","source":"arxiv","sources":["arxiv"],"published_at":"2026-06-19T06:35:52Z","category_id":"agent","cover_url":"/covers/2606_21144.png","hf_upvotes":0,"arxiv_categories":["cs.CL","cs.AI"],"summary":{"core_problem":"这篇工作讨论的不是“怎样存更多记忆”，而是“在长期个性化交互里，什么值得被写进记忆”。作者认为现有 LLM memory agent 大多默认一个统一写入规则：只要对话里出现事实，就尽量提取并保存。这个假设在短任务里问题不大，但在真实长周期场景里会导致 memory bloat：无关细节不断累积，占用检索预算和上下文窗口，最终让真正重要的信息更难被召回。更关键的是，记忆价值是角色相关、用户相关的。同一句对话，对商务助理和健身伙伴的重要性完全不同。AdaMem 试图解决的核心问题，就是如何让记忆写入策略从“尽量全记”变成“按用户偏好有选择地记”，并且能从反馈中持续修正。","importance":"对预训练本身的直接贡献有限，但对 post-train memory system 和 agent training interface 有现实意义。它把长期记忆问题从 retrieval 侧往前推了一步，强调 write control 才是部署瓶颈。这个视角很重要，因为很多记忆系统把主要精力放在更强的检索器或更长的上下文，却默认写入阶段是无害的；AdaMem 说明如果写入策略错了，后面再强的检索也只是在噪声里找答案。对基座研究员而言，启发主要有两点。第一，长期记忆不只是压缩问题，也是偏好建模问题；“什么该保留”本身需要学习。第二，反馈闭环可以不直接更新主模型，而是更新一个外部 memory policy，这是一种比全量 RL 或 continual finetuning 更轻的适配路径。它更像 memory management 层的方法，而不是新的语言建模范式。","technical_approach":"AdaMem 的核心对象是一个结构化 Memory Policy。它用 JSON 形式为每个角色 C_i 指定一段自然语言偏好描述 T_i，例如只保留业务决策和 deadline，忽略日常寒暄。整个系统按周循环，包含四步。\n\n第一步是 Daily Extraction。每天对新对话做记忆抽取时，不再使用统一 prompt，而是把当前 policy 渲染成定制化抽取指令，让 extractor LLM 按角色偏好决定写入内容。作者还加入了 Time Anchoring：在抽取 prompt 中显式提供会话绝对日期，要求模型把“明天”“下周三”这类相对时间解析成绝对日期再存储，避免长期记忆里时间语义漂移。\n\n第二步是 Weekly Evaluation。每周末用针对偏好相关信息构造的 QA 来测试系统，观察哪些问题答错。\n\n第三步是 Policy Reflection。系统分析错误来源，将失败分成两类：Recall Failure，说明对话里有信息但没被写入，当前 policy 太保守；Precision Failure，说明检索出的无关记忆干扰了回答，当前 policy 太宽松。基于这些错误，模型生成一个 patch ΔP_t 去修改 policy，而不是重写整套规则。patch-style 更新的好处是局部、可追踪，也更适合失败回滚。\n\n第四步是 Failure Rollback 和 Policy Rendering。如果新 policy 在历史验证 QA 上表现变差，就拒绝这次更新并回滚，防止 policy drift。通过这种闭环，AdaMem 试图把 memory extraction 从一次性 prompt engineering 变成持续校正的控制过程。\n\n方法上最有意思的地方不是模型结构，而是把长期记忆系统拆成了“写入策略—反馈诊断—局部修补—回滚保护”这条控制链。它没有训练新的大型记忆模块，也不依赖复杂 agent 架构，因此比较容易嵌入现有 RAG memory stack。","experiments":"实验部分包含方法评测和 benchmark 构建两层内容。作者提出了 AdaMem-Bench，用来专门测 preference-guided long-horizon memory。这个 benchmark 的设计比较贴近真实部署：多周多 session 对话、多个角色并行、角色之间存在同类语义干扰、并且提供 session-level golden memories，只把符合角色偏好的原子事实标为应保留信息，其余视为噪声。这样的标注方式比普通 QA benchmark 更适合评估写入策略是否正确。\n\n结果上，作者报告在两种 extraction LLM 和两种 feedback 模式下，AdaMem 相比基线最高带来 +9.0% QA accuracy，同时 memory volume 缩小 9%。这个组合结果比单看准确率更有说服力，因为它说明收益不是靠“多存一点”换来的，而是通过更好的写入筛选减少噪声。作者还指出，提升主要集中在 soft preference 类别，例如情绪、承诺、日程安排等。这很合理，因为这些信息往往不是显式事实三元组，统一抽取规则最容易漏掉或误存。剩余瓶颈则在于 weak feedback 下的 policy inference，也就是系统能看到答错了，但未必总能准确推断是该放宽还是收紧哪一类规则。\n\n从给出的内容看，实验更像系统行为验证，而不是大规模统计显著性研究。阅读时要留意几件事：基线是否包括“记全部”的强 RAG memory、是否比较了不同 extractor 模型的稳定性、rollback 触发频率有多高、以及 memory volume 的定义是 token 数、条目数还是检索上下文长度。若文中有按错误类型拆分的分析，那部分最能说明方法是否真的学会了 write control，而不是仅靠 prompt wording 改善。","reading_guide":"这篇适合泛读，重点放在问题设定和 benchmark 设计，不必把它当成新的模型论文来读。先看 Introduction，作者对 memory bloat 和 write control 的论证比较清楚。然后直接看 Method，抓住 weekly closed loop、Recall/Precision failure 诊断、policy patch、rollback、time anchoring 这几个部件。实验部分优先看 AdaMem-Bench 的构造原则，再看主结果表和按类别拆分的分析，判断收益来自哪里。预计 20 到 30 分钟可以读完主线；如果只想获取启发，看方法图、错误分类定义和 benchmark 示例就够了。","authors_note":""},"summary_en":{"core_problem":"The paper argues that long-term memory for personalized LLM agents is not mainly a retrieval problem but a write-control problem. Most existing systems try to remember everything: every factual statement is extracted and stored under a uniform rule. That works poorly in long-horizon deployment because memory keeps growing, irrelevant details accumulate, retrieval gets noisier, and finite context budgets are wasted on trivia. More importantly, what should be remembered is role-dependent. A manager-facing assistant and a fitness companion should preserve different parts of the same conversation. AdaMem is built to learn that selectivity: not just how to store memories, but what to store for a given user role and how to revise that policy from feedback over time.","importance":"Its direct relevance to pretraining is limited, but it is useful for researchers thinking about the interface between foundation models and persistent memory systems. The main contribution is conceptual and operational. It shifts attention from better retrieval over an ever-growing memory bank to better admission control at write time. That is a meaningful correction, because downstream retrieval quality is bounded by the quality of what was written in the first place. For LLM systems work, the paper also shows a lightweight adaptation route: instead of updating the base model or running full continual finetuning, one can update an external memory policy through a feedback loop. This is closer to memory management than to a new modeling paradigm, but it is a practical idea for long-horizon agents.","technical_approach":"$6d","experiments":"$6e","reading_guide":"This is best read as a systems paper on memory control, not as a model-architecture paper. Start with the introduction, where the memory-bloat argument is laid out clearly. Then read the method section with attention to five components: the weekly closed loop, the recall-versus-precision failure taxonomy, patch-based policy updates, rollback, and time anchoring. The main findings are that heterogeneous teams can improve accuracy by up to 44% when models are assigned to suitable roles, while reversing the same pair can reduce accuracy by 36%. Heterogeneous teams often occupy the Pareto frontier and can match the strongest homogeneous team at 1.4x to 12x lower per-task cost. Planner and executor upgrade returns differ by up to 40% across domains. A three-role plan-verify-execute pilot adds up to 9.4% accuracy over the strongest two-agent baseline at comparable cost.","reading_guide":"Skim in 15–25 minutes.
